title: Tag-triggered release publishing: assets, checksums, provenance, notes
description:
Wire the matrix into the release. The CI workflow added for 0.2.0 already triggers on tags matching v*, so the hook point exists; what is missing is publishing.

- On a v* tag: run the build matrix (022.2), then the per-artifact verification (022.3), then create/attach to the GitHub Release.
- Attach per-artifact SHA256 checksums. A dlopen'ed module downloaded from the internet and loaded into a long-running desktop process deserves at least a checksum, and ideally GitHub build-provenance attestation.
- Generate release notes that state the two facts a user needs before downloading: the glibc floor and the waybar ABI version the artifacts were built against (from 022.1). "Works with waybar" without a version is not a claim anyone can act on.
- Refuse to publish if any verification step fails. A half-published release with 3 of 4 targets is worse than none.
- Decide whether the tag job also asserts that the tag matches the Cargo.toml version. v0.2.0 was tagged by hand against a manually bumped version; nothing currently stops those two from disagreeing.

Note the existing release ceremony gap: v0.2.0 is tagged and pushed but has no GitHub Release object at all. Decide whether this job backfills 0.2.0 or starts at the next tag.
acceptance_criteria: Pushing a v* tag yields a GitHub Release with all four verified artifact pairs plus checksums, and notes stating the glibc floor and waybar ABI version; a failed verification blocks publication; tag and Cargo.toml version are asserted to agree.

title: Verify each artifact in its target container (dlopen, not just ldd)
description:
Verify each artifact INSIDE its target distro container before it is ever published. A broken prebuilt module fails inside the user's bar, where the diagnostics are worst.

Four checks per artifact:

1. ldd -r for unresolved symbols against the container's own GTK3/EGL stack.
2. Exported CFFI surface present: wbcffi_init, wbcffi_deinit, wbcffi_update, wbcffi_refresh, wbcffi_doaction, and the wbcffi_version data symbol.
3. glibc floor assertion: the highest GLIBC_ versioned symbol referenced must not exceed the floor declared by 022.1. This is the check that stops the floor from silently creeping up whenever a build image is refreshed.
4. A real dlopen. This is the one that matters and the one ldd cannot do: libepoxy is NOT in DT_NEEDED, because GL entry points are resolved at runtime from the libepoxy waybar has already loaded. So an artifact can satisfy every link-time dependency and still fail at render time. A tiny C or Rust harness that dlopens the .so, reads wbcffi_version and calls dlsym on the entry points is enough to catch the realistic breakage.

Do NOT attempt a pixel-comparison render here. Containers have no Terminus font and no compositor; the existing CI render-smoke job already covers "does it rasterise". This job answers "is this artifact loadable on this distro".
acceptance_criteria: Every published artifact has passed unresolved-symbol, exported-symbol, glibc-floor and dlopen checks inside a container of the distro it claims to support; the release job refuses to publish if any check fails.

title: Containerised release build matrix: Arch + Debian unstable, x86_64 + aarch64
description:
Produce the 4 artifact pairs. Build each inside a container of the target distro so the glibc floor and the GTK3 stack are the target's by construction rather than by hope.

- Arch: an archlinux base-devel container; install gtk3, pango, cairo, libepoxy, mesa (for libEGL) plus rust.
- Debian unstable: a debian:unstable container; the dev package list already exists in mise.toml (build-essential pkg-config libgtk-3-dev libepoxy-dev libegl-dev libgl-dev).
- aarch64: GitHub now offers native arm64 Linux runners for public repos — VERIFY the current runner label before writing it in, and prefer native over qemu; cross-compiling this is painful because the -sys crates want target-arch pkg-config and headers, which is exactly what a native runner gives for free.

Reuse the existing rust-toolchain.toml pin so the release build uses the same toolchain as CI — no second source of truth.

Strip the artifacts. They are 7.4M (.so) and 7.2M (CLI) unstripped, which is ~29M per target pair and ~59M per release across four targets, nearly all debug symbols. Either add strip to the release profile in Cargo.toml or strip as a separate build step; if the profile is changed, note that it also affects local dev builds and the "task install" flow.

Name artifacts so the target is unambiguous from the filename alone, e.g. libpwetty_box-ARCH-x86_64.so / libpwetty_box-DEBIAN-aarch64.so (pick a scheme; the point is that a downloaded bare libpwetty_box.so is unidentifiable once it is sitting in a user's lib dir).
acceptance_criteria: A workflow_dispatch run produces stripped .so + pwetty for all four targets as uploaded artifacts, each built in its target distro container, with the toolchain coming from rust-toolchain.toml.

title: Pin and document the binary compatibility contract
description:
DESIGN GATE — settle this before building anything, because every later choice (which container, which runner, what the release notes may claim) falls out of it. A prebuilt dlopen'ed module makes promises; right now none of them are written down.

Decide and record, in the README next to the existing module_path guidance:

1. GLIBC FLOOR. The v0.2.0 build already requires >= 2.39, purely because of the host that built it. Nothing declares this and nothing checks it, so a user on an older distro gets a dlopen failure with no useful message. Pick the floor deliberately: the oldest glibc among the distros we claim to support, then BUILD ON THAT and assert it in CI (highest GLIBC_ symbol version must be <= the declared floor). Building on the newest and hoping is how this silently rots.

2. WAYBAR ABI. Compatibility is mediated by the wbcffi_version data symbol, defined by waybar-cffi 0.1.1. Determine which waybar releases accept that value and state the supported range. Without this, 'works with waybar' is an unverified claim on a component that gets loaded into someone's bar.

3. GTK3 STACK. All DT_NEEDED entries are stable sonames (libgtk-3.so.0, libcairo.so.2, ...), so no per-version pinning is needed — but say so explicitly, since it is the reason a single artifact per distro is viable at all.

4. THE INVISIBLE ONE. libepoxy is not in DT_NEEDED; GL is resolved at runtime from waybar's already-loaded copy. Document it, because it means a user can satisfy every ldd dependency and still fail at render time if their waybar was built without epoxy.

Also decide what happens on mismatch: today the failure mode is presumably a bare dlopen error inside waybar. Even a one-line 'built for glibc >= X' in the README is a large improvement over that.
acceptance_criteria: README states the glibc floor, the supported waybar ABI/version range, the GTK3 soname expectations and the runtime-epoxy caveat; CI asserts the built artifact does not exceed the declared glibc floor.

title: Release engineering: ship prebuilt module artifacts for modern-glibc distros
description:
Today the only way to get this module is to build it: clone, install GTK3/epoxy/EGL dev headers, cargo build --release, point module_path at a local target dir. v0.2.0 is tagged but ships nothing. Goal: attach prebuilt libpwetty_box.so + the pwetty CLI to each release for modern-glibc distros (Arch, Debian unstable) on x86_64 and aarch64.

WHAT THE BINARY ACTUALLY COUPLES TO (measured on the v0.2.0 x86_64 build, not assumed):

- DT_NEEDED: libgtk-3.so.0, libgdk-3.so.0, libpangocairo-1.0.so.0, libpango-1.0.so.0, libcairo.so.2, libgobject-2.0.so.0, libglib-2.0.so.0, libEGL.so.1, libgcc_s.so.1, libm.so.6, libc.so.6. All stable sonames, so the GTK3 stack is a smaller risk than it looks.
- libepoxy is deliberately NOT in DT_NEEDED. GL entry points are resolved at RUNTIME out of the libepoxy that waybar has already loaded in-process (see the epoxy/libloading note in Cargo.toml). Consequence: ldd -r cannot see this dependency, so artifact verification must dlopen, not just link-check.
- Highest versioned glibc symbol referenced: GLIBC_2.39. So the artifact already requires glibc >= 2.39, and that floor is set by whatever host builds it — silently. This is the single biggest footgun in the whole effort.
- Exported CFFI surface: wbcffi_init, wbcffi_deinit, wbcffi_update, wbcffi_refresh, wbcffi_doaction, plus the wbcffi_version DATA symbol that waybar reads to accept or reject the module. That symbol makes waybar-ABI compatibility machine-checkable per artifact.
- waybar-cffi 0.1.1 is what defines that ABI.
- Unstripped sizes: 7.4M for the .so, 7.2M for the CLI.

SCOPE: 4 artifact pairs (Arch + Debian unstable) x (x86_64 + aarch64), built in containers matching the target distro, verified in that same container, checksummed, and attached to the GitHub release by the existing tag-triggered CI.

NOT IN SCOPE: old-glibc support. No manylinux-style oldest-glibc build, no static glibc, no vendoring GTK. Deliberately excluded per the modern-distro framing.
design: Containerised per-distro builds rather than one 'universal' Linux artifact. A single build cannot honestly claim both Arch and Debian-unstable compatibility, because the glibc floor comes from the build host and nothing in the artifact declares it. Building inside the target distro's own container makes the claim true by construction and makes the floor auditable. The alternative — build once on the oldest supported glibc and let symbol versioning carry it forward — is the standard trick and would work, but it means maintaining a separate old build image whose whole purpose is compatibility we just said is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: A pushed vN.N.N tag produces a GitHub release carrying, for each of the 4 targets, a stripped libpwetty_box.so and pwetty binary plus checksums; each artifact has been dlopen-verified inside its target distro container; and the release notes state the glibc floor and the waybar ABI version the artifacts were built against.

title: Idle time label can overflow its reserved slot and collide with the folder name
description:
The idle age label drawn beside the fade bar is never measured against the width the status embed actually reserves, so a longer-than-expected idle_ago paints over the folder text to its right.

The slot is a fixed cap_h * 3.0 (embed_ew, src/lib.rs:615) and the label starts at bar_cx + cap_h * 0.85, leaving roughly 1.6 * cap_h for text drawn at ~0.92 * cap_h monospace bold — about 3 characters. 170335f removed the cr.text_extents(ago) call that was the only thing capable of measuring it, and its replacement doc comment now claims 'The whole badge lives in the status embed's reserved width, so the time never spills into the folder/next tile' — which is not enforced anywhere.

Verified by offscreen render on the current tree: idle_ago '12m' sits clear of the folder with a visible gap, while '120m' runs straight into 'dotfiles' with no separation. Longer values ('2 hours') are worse.

Fix either by clamping/ellipsizing the label against the reserved ew, or by feeding the measured text width back into embed_ew so the layout reserves what the badge actually needs.
notes: Found while closing epic pwetty-box-rs-ie9; unrelated to that work, introduced by 170335f. Shares a root with pwetty-box-rs-00i (both concern the idle label added by that commit). Reference renders are in ~/.cache/pwetty-qa/shots (adhoc-ago.png vs claude-idle.png).

title: idle_ago parsing: non-integer or worded labels silently read as 'fresh'
description:
idle_minutes (src/lib.rs:1322) splits idle_ago at the first non-ASCII-digit char and matches the remainder against h/hr/hrs/d/s/sec, falling through to 'minutes' for anything else. So any label that is not <integer><known-suffix> degrades to a tiny minute count and idle_age_color paints it FULL WHITE — the 'just idled' signal — which is the exact opposite of the truth for an old session.

Verified on the current tree by reading the function and by offscreen render:
  '1.5h'   -> splits at '.', n=1, suffix '.5h' hits the _ arm -> 1 min  -> white (should be full red: 90 min)
  '2 hours'-> suffix 'hours' -> _ arm                          -> 2 min  -> white
  '1h30m'  -> suffix 'h30m'  -> _ arm                          -> 1 min  -> white

Nothing rejects these: tiles/claude/schema.json types idle_ago as a free-form string ('keep it short') with only '12m'/'2h' as examples. The failure direction is the harmful one — a two-day-idle session reads as just-touched.

Root cause is arguably the two sources of truth: the fade CELLS use the numeric idle_level (0-6, already in the payload), while the LABEL colour is re-derived by parsing the human-facing string. Deriving the colour from idle_level, or adding an explicit numeric minutes field, deletes the parser and the bug class with it.
notes: Found while closing epic pwetty-box-rs-ie9; unrelated to that work, introduced by 170335f 'feat: fading cooldowns'. Related: pwetty-box-rs-hzh is the bead that specified this feature and is still OPEN despite being implemented, and its text is now stale (it specifies white->red topping out at 1h, while the implementation continues into bright/dark purple across 3-9h).

title: Offscreen render check: two-app and mixed tile shapes
description:
Visually verify the new layouts without touching the live compositor. Use examples/render_tile.rs with EGL_PLATFORM=surfaceless LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 - it spawns and kills nothing, which is the standing rule in this repo after the nested-niri logout incidents.

Check specifically that (a) the two rows app icons come out the same size - they are row-leading embeds so both should take the line_h*0.62 cap from cap_at (src/lib.rs:589-601), (b) the 4-line block still clears 96px, (c) an unpushed arrow badge on a session row does not inflate its neighbour row.

(a) icon sizes match across rows: a twin-app-row payload is pixel-identical to itself shifted by exactly one row pitch (42px = 2 lines) — 7 differing px, worst channel delta 19/255, pure antialiasing from the fractional 7.5px top pad — versus ~700+ differing px at plus-or-minus 1px, so both leading embeds take the same cap. (b) the 4-line block clears 96px: non-active two-row tiles top out at ink y=88, i.e. 7px bottom clearance; active tiles reach y=94 but that is the card border, identical to the pre-existing duo.   `status state=.. level=.. ago=..` + folder + optional unpushed arrow   (session row)
  `icon name=.. size=1.1` + app name                                    (app row)
each followed by a newline and `tickerbox width=180` wrapping the title at size=small. One row keeps the current single-session and single-window layouts byte-identical, watermark included.

Also fix icon-name robustness while here: the current test for a slash in app_icon blows up on an undefined app_icon. Hoist it to {% set ico = row.app_icon | default("app") %} and branch on ico, so the path-vs-bundled-name split can never see undefined.

title: Window tile: two-app support (unified items[] rows)
description:
A window tile renders exactly one app today: the is_claude=false branch of the format string in tiles/claude/tile.json = big dimmed watermark icon + shortcut + app name + wrapped title. A niri desktop can hold two windows and the tile has no way to say so. Worse, the schema allOf/if-else makes a MIXED desktop (one Claude session plus one plain app) unrepresentable: is_claude=false requires app/app_icon, else requires sessions.

Design agreed 2026-07-29: unify sessions[] and the flat app/app_icon/title fields into ONE items[] array of rows (max 2). Row kinds: a Claude session row (status mascot + folder + unpushed) or an app row (inline app icon + app name). Two rows render as the EXISTING dual-session geometry - shared shortcut digit in a `gutter` element, one `tickerbox` title per row. One row keeps the current single layouts unchanged. The data picks the layout; the caller never does.

Renderer facts that shaped this (the agreed scope needs NO Rust):
- inline `icon name=.. size=N` works at any position, sized cap_h * size (icon_size, src/lib.rs:530), and a row-leading embed gets a stable line_h*0.62 cap (cap_at, src/lib.rs:589-601) - the same mechanism that keeps dual-session mascots matching across rows.
- 4 lines (2 rows x header+ticker) already fit 240x96: line_h=21, top_pad=7.5, total 91.5 (src/lib.rs:648-649, 701-726). Proven by the existing dual-session tile.
- the `icon watermark` path is deliberately NOT reused for dual rows: watermark_draw is a single Option detected only at lines[0][0] (src/lib.rs:663-676), so two artworks need Rust - and a Claude row would always show kitty, which carries zero information. Split out as the deferred artwork child.

NOTE: bd show renders markdown and swallows raw angle brackets - keep template tag names backticked in these descriptions.
design: Rejected alternatives: (a) two split watermarks - needs watermark_draw Option->Vec plus half= placement, and 120px per half leaves no room for titles; (b) watermark plus small companion badge - cheapest but drops the second app name and title; (c) keeping sessions[] and adding a parallel windows[] array - works for two apps but still cannot express a mixed desktop, which was the deciding factor. items[] subsumes the windows[] variant at the same cost.
acceptance_criteria: A two-window tile renders both app icons, names and tickered titles. A mixed tile renders one session row and one app row in the same geometry. Existing single-session, dual-session and single-window payloads render unchanged.
close_reason: All four children resolved: ie9.1 (template), ie9.2 (schema+samples), ie9.3 (offscreen render check) done; ie9.4 closed WON'T DO from rendered evidence. Acceptance criteria met: a two-window tile renders both app icons, names and tickered titles; a mixed tile renders one session row and one app row in the same geometry; and existing single-session, dual-session and single-window payloads render byte-identical markup to before (verified by cmp against the HEAD template, twice, with independent harnesses). No Rust renderer changes were needed, as the epic predicted. Added a permanent guard the repo lacked: samples are now schema-validated in cargo test (boon dev-dep), plus a counterexample test so the relaxed anyOf cannot rot into a vacuously permissive schema — pwetty check only ever proved samples RENDER, never that they match the contract.

title: Streaming/push exec for sub-second tile refresh (cffi consumer)
description:
Filed by the claude-status consumer (~/Perso/claude-status-db). CONTEXT: claude-status drives a row of per-desktop cffi/pwetty tiles via exec; it needs the active-desktop highlight to update within a few hundred ms on a niri desktop switch. The consumer-side exec is already ~3ms (a cache read), so the only remaining latency is pwetty refresh cadence.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR (src/content.rs from_config): a thread loops run_command(exec) via std .output (which blocks until the process EXITS and captures all stdout) then sleeps interval WHOLE seconds (Duration from_secs; interval 0 = run once). So refresh is poll-only with a 1s floor and no push path; the active tile lags up to ~1s on switch.

ASK: a streaming/push exec mode. Spawn the command ONCE and read stdout line-by-line via BufReader lines(), calling ContentStore::set per line, instead of .output once per interval. The existing 150ms redraw timer + dirty flag (src/lib.rs near line 264) then repaints within ~150ms of each pushed line. One long-lived process per tile: no respawn churn, no polling. Suggest gating with a stream:true flag (default false) so the current interval poll path is byte-for-byte unchanged; or treat interval 0 plus a continuously-emitting command as streaming.

PRODUCER CONTRACT: the command stays alive and prints one newline-delimited JSON object whenever data changes; pwetty applies each line as new content (same parse_data). On EOF/exit keep last content (optionally restart with backoff); skip malformed lines.

ACCEPTANCE: a streaming-command tile repaints within ~150ms of a new stdout line; existing interval tiles unaffected; a streaming process that exits does not busy-loop.

ALTERNATIVES (less preferred): fractional/millisecond interval; or honor the waybar signal refresh.

CONSUMER READINESS: claude-status will ship a tile-watch producer (emits a fresh line on every desktop change via an event-updated cache + inotify) the moment this lands. Consumer-side tracking: claude-status-db-9h4.
close_reason: Implemented stream:true push mode in content.rs (spawn-once + BufReader lines + set per line; EOF keeps last content, respawns after 1s backoff; blank lines skipped). Unconditional 150ms dirty poll repaints; no lib.rs change. Docs + 2 tests added. Gates green (45 tests, clippy, pwetty check).

title: Stream exec children outlive a hard-killed waybar
description: content.rs kills the stream child's process group from Drop, which only runs on a waybar reload (SIGUSR2). When waybar is SIGTERMed or restarted (kill + respawn), the sh -c wrapper and its producer (e.g. claude-status tile-watch) are reparented to systemd --user and live until their next stdout write hits EPIPE; quiet producers (empty desktops) never write, so they leak forever. Observed: 100+ orphan groups after a few restarts. Fix idea: prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM) in the child via pre_exec, or have the producer poll for stdout close.

title: Distro-native packaging: AUR PKGBUILD, optionally a .deb
description:
Distro-native packaging as the better long-term delivery, filed as a sibling to the raw-artifact track rather than instead of it.

A bare .so from a release page gives the user no dependency resolution, no upgrade path and no uninstall. An AUR PKGBUILD (Arch) and optionally a .deb for Debian unstable declare their gtk3/pango/cairo/libepoxy/mesa dependencies properly, let the distro's own package manager satisfy them, and remove the glibc-floor question entirely because the package is built against the distro it installs on.

This does not replace 022.2 through 022.4: a release page artifact is still the fastest path for someone who just wants to try the module, and packaging needs somewhere to fetch a versioned source tarball from — which a tagged release provides.

If this track is adopted, revisit whether all four raw artifact pairs are still worth carrying, or whether the release page can drop to source tarball plus checksums and let packages do the rest.

title: CI: verify the rust-version 1.88 MSRV claim, or correct it
description:
Cargo.toml declares rust-version = 1.88 but nothing tests it. Only 1.92 is installed on the dev box (rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.92, and its own comment says waybar-cffi needs >=1.85 and femtovg >=1.88), so the 1.88 floor is an assertion no one has exercised — and transitive deps raise their own MSRVs over time without asking.

The CI added in the 0.2.0 commit deliberately has no MSRV job, because a job asserting an unverified claim is a guess that would just go red.

Do one of: (a) add a gates-style job with RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.88 running cargo check --all-targets (RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN takes precedence over rust-toolchain.toml, so the pin does not fight it), and keep it green by bumping rust-version when a dep forces it; or (b) if 1.88 no longer builds, raise rust-version to whatever actually works and drop the fiction.

Cheap either way: it is a check, not a full test run.
notes: Split out of the CI/0.2.0 work rather than shipped unverified. If (a), note that cargo's own resolver honours rust-version, so a too-low MSRV claim can also mislead dependency resolution for consumers.

title: Per-row watermark artwork on app rows (deferred, cosmetic)
description:
DEFERRED cosmetic variant of the two-row layout: give each APP row its own medium dimmed artwork (~0.44h) anchored to that rows band, right-aligned, replacing the inline icon. Session rows get none on purpose - a Claude row would always show kitty, which carries no information. That asymmetry is the whole reason this is split out.

Renderer work, all inside flow_layout in src/lib.rs:
1. multiply the hardcoded wm_h = h * 0.92 (src/lib.rs:673) by icon_size(), so a watermark icon can take a size= multiplier. One line.
2. watermark_draw: Option becomes Vec, with detection widened from "first embed of line 0" (src/lib.rs:666) to "first embed of any line", each anchored to its own vertical band. The bands are already computable - heights is precomputed at src/lib.rs:701-721 before any drawing - so this is bookkeeping, not restructuring. Roughly 30-40 lines.
3. generalize the leading-embed skip at src/lib.rs:812 (hero and li == 0 and ii == 0) to any line whose first embed was consumed as a background.
4. optional alpha= attr so 0.22 stops being hardcoded; draw_icon_alpha already takes an alpha.

Ticker interaction: draw_ticker is a hard cr.clip() with no border and no edge fade (src/lib.rs:1447-1449), so a 180px row beside a 120px row shows two different hard truncation edges whenever both titles scroll. Fix in the template, not Rust: trim EVERY row in a tile to 120 when ANY row carries artwork. Differing widths between separate cards do not read as anything.

Judge it offscreen before deciding the 40 lines are worth it - with artwork limited to app rows it carries the same information as the inline icon, just larger. Depends on ie9.3 so the render harness and reference shots already exist when this is judged.
design: Deferred rather than dropped: the information argument says the inline icon is sufficient, but the artwork may still be worth it purely as a look. Decide from rendered output, not from the description.
close_reason: WON'T DO — judged from rendered output exactly as the bead asked. The inline icon at size 1.1 reads clearly in every two-row shot (duo-window, mixed, twin-app-row) and carries the same information artwork would. The cost is not only the 30-40 lines in flow_layout (watermark_draw Option to Vec, per-band anchoring, generalizing the leading-embed skip): by the bead's own ticker analysis, artwork forces trimming EVERY row's tickerbox from 180 to 120px to avoid two mismatched hard truncation edges — a permanent ~33% title-width loss on all two-row tiles, bought purely for a look. Not worth it. Reopen if the look is wanted on its own merits; the render harness and reference shots now exist, so re-judging is cheap.
